title: Measurement of Length and Motion

standard_text: Need for standard units of measurement; SI unit of length; correct way of measuring length with a scale; measuring curved lines; motion and rest, reference point; linear, circular and oscillatory (periodic) motion (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 5).

key_big: The SI unit of length is the metre.
body_html:
How to think about it

Handspans and cubits are different for different people, so we use standard units. The SI unit of length is the metre (m): 1 km = 1000 m, 1 m = 100 cm and 1 cm = 10 mm. Read a scale with your eye straight above the mark; if the zero is broken, start from another mark and subtract.

An object is in motion if its position changes with time compared to a reference point. Motion along a straight line is linear (rectilinear), motion along a circle is circular, and to-and-fro motion is oscillatory. Motion that repeats after equal times is periodic.

Example

Convert 3.5 m into cm.

1 m = 100 cm

3.5 × 100

Answer: 350 cm

Example

A swing moving to and fro shows…

back and forth about a point

Answer: oscillatory motion

Common mistakes

  • Multiplying when converting a small unit to a bigger one.
  • Reading a scale from an angle.
  • Forgetting to subtract the starting mark.

faq.q: Why do we need standard units?
faq.a: So that everybody gets the same result when measuring the same object.

faq.q: What is the difference between circular and oscillatory motion?
faq.a: In circular motion an object moves along a circle; in oscillatory motion it moves to and fro about a fixed position.
